comparator.serving_path: raw audio through the bf16 mmproj, -c 49152 -np 3
comparator.what_the_comparator_sends: the sealed 24 kHz bytes verbatim (core/model/transport.py base64s the file and declares format 'wav'); the 24 -> 16 kHz conversion happens inside llama.cpp's miniaudio decoder, not in this study

id_rule: <sealed id>@16k+ts2; the sealed key is recovered by splitting on the FIRST '@' (reproduction.esb_reference.published_segment_key), so the paired join against the sealed comparator is exact and no id collides with the comparator population's
rule: every sealed 24 kHz mono int16 release wav decoded to 16 kHz mono int16 through reproduction.obs_loop.decode_parent_pcm -- librosa.load(sr=16000, mono=True) at res_type 'soxr_hq' (librosa 0.11.0 / soxr 1.1.0), then clip(rint(float32 * 32767), -32768, 32767) to int16; nothing is trimmed, nothing is normalized, no channel is dropped and the sample count is the exact 2/3 the rate ratio requires; then exactly 2.0 s of digital silence appended to the 16 kHz standardized clip -- 32,000 zero samples through the PINNED Earnings-22 transform('tail-silence-2s', ...); nothing is removed, no standardized sample is altered and the sample rate is never changed
split_role_basis: The SAME frozen 400-row Audio2Tool discovery split (50 per tier over all eight tiers) the sealed official-protocol replication flew, re-encoded by one deterministic rule from the sealed WAV bytes. The split was already exposed by A0 and stays discovery. No evaluation query text, gold tool name, argument or tool registry row is opened here.
what_it_is_for: cell (b): the silence tail on STANDARDIZED bytes, which replaces the cross-carrier preregistration's 24 kHz-based @ts2 Audio2Tool cell if and only if cell (a) admits the standardization
